extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers; journalists and government/public information personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural requirements for manuscripts, speeches, press releases and other public-information material produced by the U.S. Department of Defense, including clearance, timing, authorship and organizational rules. These are reported as a Defense Department order described in a news article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive contribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Material must 'constitute a constructive contribution to the primary mission of the Defense Department.' (Described in the order as the 'constructive' criterion for writings.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to manuscripts, speeches, press releases, photographs or 'other information.' Items must not only be security-cleared but also judged to make a constructive contribution to the department's mission. The order says articles must pass the test for constructiveness (a test in effect since 1949) and meet whatever additional standards the Secretary sets up to ensure they 'constitute a constructive contribution.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Security clearance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All matter prepared for publication 'must be submitted for review' and 'must be cleared for security, as in the past.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security clearance remains required in addition to the constructive-content determination. Materials prepared for publication must be submitted for review to the Secretary's office and cleared for security before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-day pre-release submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Speeches, releases, etc., 'must be submitted for clearance three days before their scheduled release date.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explicitly requires submission of material three days prior to the scheduled release to allow time for review and determinations (security and constructive contribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on pre-clearance submission to outside publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: The order 'forbids the submission of manuscripts to magazine editors and the like before they have been cleared at the Pentagon.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and departmental personnel may not send manuscripts or other material to external publishers or editors until the Pentagon clearance process is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal coverage/scope of the order
rubrics_metrics.description: The order 'covers every employee of the Defense Department and every member of the military services.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to civilian personnel as well as military members; the Secretary's earlier direction discouraging senior officers from lending their names to articles about their official duties is noted as complementary policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use civilians to head public information services
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army, Navy and Air Force are ordered 'to use civilians instead of officers to head their public information services.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These civilians would be responsible to the Secretaries of Defense/Service and would handle clearance procedures; this is intended to shift public-information leadership away from uniformed officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction in military public-information personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Directive to reduce 'the number of military persons engaged in information duties be reduced one-third to one-half.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order notes an assessment that services had not fully complied with previous instructions to reduce such personnel; provides numeric staffing context (e.g., rosters and counts cited) and is linked to shifting responsibilities to civilians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of off-the-record talks and lending names
rubrics_metrics.description: The order 'should discourage such off-the-record talks' and previously directed that senior officers be discouraged from lending their names to articles about their official duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy aims to limit informal or unofficial disclosures (e.g., off-the-record briefings) and reduce the practice of senior officers lending official credibility to articles on their duties without proper clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to inform the public within limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department has 'an obligation to inform the public within the limitations of security and policy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a guiding principle balancing openness with security and policy constraints; it frames the clearance and constructive-contribution requirements as consistent with the obligation to inform the public.
